cohort: 600 patients who underwent labor induction with either a low-volume or high-volume Foley catheter
finding: Labor induction with a high-volume Foley catheter was associated with a higher percentage of vaginal deliveries, shorter time to delivery, and lower need for oxytocin augmentation compared to a low-volume Foley catheter.
mod_finding: Patients who received a high-volume Foley catheter had statistically significantly more vaginal deliveries.
